**Title:** Which Dollar Broke? Separating Token Failures from Platform-Ledger Failures in Web Dollar Markets

**Abstract (299 words):**

In October 2018 our monitor flagged Bitfinex's dollar as trading below bank money 3 days before its deposit freeze was reported and 6.5 months before regulators disclosed the loss behind it. Web price feeds and oracles miss such signals because they average exchange prices as if all used the same dollar; CoinMarketCap dropped Bitfinex from its bitcoin average by hand only in May 2019, 7 months later. Some exchanges quote stablecoins; others quote balances in their own ledger, convertible to bank money only through their banks. When that link breaks, the exchange's dollar drifts, and feeds read it as a price move or a stablecoin failure. We tell the two apart by pricing the exchange's own dollar with the law of one price across exchanges and triangular arbitrage within one. Because bitcoin has no peg, its price gap between the troubled exchange and one whose banking still works measures the ledger's loss of value, and the rest of a stablecoin's dislocation belongs to the token. We accept the split only when an unrelated asset shows the same gap, the implied token price matches its direct price elsewhere, and its internal cross-rates hold. In banking cut-offs on three exchanges from 2017 to 2023, the dollar broke on Bitfinex and Binance.US but barely moved on Binance's sterling and euro rails. On Bitfinex it fell by up to 844 basis points, with bitcoin and ether agreeing to within 7.2 and cross-rates holding to within 8. On both it moved from a discount to a premium before recovering. A multi-exchange bitcoin index was off by 100 basis points or more for 2,826 hours, and dropping exchange-hours our monitor flags removes 88% of them. In the March 2023 USD Coin run it instead blames the token for all but 6%. All findings are descriptive.

**Suggested keywords:** stablecoins; platform money; exchange ledgers; price feeds and oracles; Web measurement; natural experiment; reproducibility
